requirements.requirement: ProtocolSpec requires units, scaling, signedness, side effects, retry semantics, and source anchors; unresolved critical fields prevent dependent checks or generation.
requirements.acceptance: Feed missing and contradictory fields; verify a structured ambiguity with cited source anchors.
requirements.rationale: A plausible guess about scaling or side effects is worse than an explicit unsupported field.

requirements.requirement: Two reviewed fictional protocol fixtures have typed reference drivers exposing only supported operations; generation is optional.
requirements.acceptance: Compare reference API and annotations to capability lists; unsupported operations have explicit outcomes. Use hand-authored or checked-in candidates for the offline demo.
requirements.rationale: Two deliberately different protocols expose ASCII and register assumptions without claiming broad device support.

requirements.requirement: Signed register and voltage scaling match golden wire vectors exactly.
requirements.acceptance: Check FB2E → -12.34 C and 1.250 V → 04E2 against hand-calculated constants.
requirements.rationale: Independent constants expose signedness and unit errors that a driver and emulator could otherwise share.

requirements.requirement: Framing and parsing reject truncated, overlong, nonfinite, malformed, and trailing input.
requirements.acceptance: Inject each malformed response without calling production parsers in the oracle.
requirements.rationale: Malformed traffic must not become a plausible measurement.

requirements.requirement: Read retry is bounded; uncertain side-effecting writes are never replayed automatically.
requirements.acceptance: Fake clock and counted transport prove two maximum read attempts and one write.
requirements.rationale: A lost acknowledgment does not prove a write failed; replaying it may repeat an action.

requirements.requirement: Errors, cancellation, and close preserve operation ordering and typed outcomes.
requirements.acceptance: Cancel a pending read then attempt another; no stale response can be reused. Close twice.
requirements.rationale: Late responses and cancellation are common ways to associate a valid value with the wrong request.

requirements.requirement: The oracle rejects six seeded driver defects.
requirements.acceptance: Unsigned decode, factor-of-1000 voltage, swapped bytes, blind write retry, swallowed device error, stale response reuse each fail at least one assertion.
requirements.rationale: A suite that accepts known defects is not credible evidence of conformance.

requirements.requirement: At least 20 conformance cases and 10 missing/contradictory-source cases have explicit decisions; enabled model extraction also receives instruction-injection cases.
requirements.acceptance: A manifest enumerates cases and expected decisions; source text cannot alter evaluator rules or run shell commands.
requirements.rationale: Coverage must include decisions to abstain, not just normal command responses.

requirements.requirement: Offline demo requires neither a model key nor physical I/O and preserves a failed attempt.
requirements.acceptance: Run with credentials absent and network disabled; inspect manifest and failure report.
requirements.rationale: A test engineer should be able to evaluate the tool without buying a device or model subscription.

requirements.requirement: Generated code cannot edit evaluation inputs or access credentials/network.
requirements.acceptance: Isolation tests attempt forbidden writes and egress and hit the timeout limit; report unavailable isolation as blocked.
requirements.rationale: Optional candidate execution cannot be allowed to alter the evidence used to judge it.
requirements.applies_when: Only when executing untrusted generated code; unavailable isolation disables this feature, not the core test kit.

requirements.requirement: Reports trace results to protocol source, candidate hash, oracle version, and commands.
requirements.acceptance: Verify artifact hashes and recompute expected output from a fresh checkout.
requirements.rationale: Engineers need to see the actual bytes and requirement behind a verdict to debug a failure.

requirements.requirement: The public package passes lint, type checks, meaningful tests, and documented installation.
requirements.acceptance: Fresh environment follows README and repeats the offline demonstration.
requirements.rationale: An installable maintained package is more useful than a notebook tied to its author's machine.

requirements.requirement: Compare a pinned PyMeasure expected_protocol/PyVISA-sim baseline with the proposed fault kit on the same driver operations.
requirements.rationale: Existing tools already cover normal protocol testing; duplication is not a useful portfolio result.
requirements.acceptance: Record setup steps, handwritten adapter/test code size, supported fault cases, and missing semantics in docs/BASELINE.md. If the baseline meets all needs, implement a small compatible extension or examples package instead of a new driver framework.

requirements.requirement: Test at least one pinned, real public PyMeasure driver without rewriting its implementation, through an injectable transport adapter.
requirements.rationale: The original fictional devices alone did not demonstrate adoption by an existing engineering codebase.
requirements.acceptance: M0 chooses a redistributable public driver and cites its commit plus public protocol documentation. Exercise at least three operations and three distinct fault cases; save exact requests and responses. Do not label the result physical validation or a reproduced upstream bug without matching evidence.

requirements.requirement: A declarative fault schedule supports timeout, fragmented response, malformed response, device error, and late response after cancellation or timeout.
requirements.rationale: Repeatable negative cases are the main added value over a canned happy-path emulator.
requirements.acceptance: Each fault has onset, affected operation, expected outcome, and deterministic transcript. The adapter reports unsupported capabilities explicitly; upstream synchronous APIs need not pretend to support async cancellation.

requirements.requirement: Expose a pytest fixture/API that exercises supported existing-driver adapters without requiring a new hardware abstraction layer.
requirements.rationale: Requiring a driver rewrite would erase most of the adoption benefit.
requirements.acceptance: A separate consumer package runs a driver conformance test using only public APIs. Its upstream source remains unchanged; unsupported framing or retry behaviors are reported rather than silently treated as tested.

requirements.requirement: Compare two run reports by operation and requirement with readable byte-level differences.
requirements.rationale: A comparison makes driver and dependency upgrades easier to review.
requirements.acceptance: A single changed terminator, scale, and retry count each produce a specific diff; unchanged data produce no regression.
requirements.applies_when: If selected after Must requirements pass

requirements.requirement: Add manual-to-spec generation and bounded model repair after the deterministic conformance tool works.
requirements.rationale: Agent-assisted development already demonstrates the intended portfolio skill; a product model is optional.
requirements.acceptance: Any enabled experiment retains all attempts, freezes the oracle first, uses at most three repair attempts by default, and labels replay separately from live evaluation. No credentials or API budget means this experiment is not run.
requirements.applies_when: If selected after Must requirements pass

requirements.requirement: Publish a versioned input and result schema, stable requirement IDs, public Python API, and a scriptable CLI with clear failure semantics.
requirements.rationale: CI must not confuse an unsupported check or crashed evaluator with a valid result.
requirements.acceptance: For normal check commands: exit 0 only when every applicable required check passes; exit 1 for violations; exit 2 for invalid, incomplete, unsupported, or failed execution. Results preserve individual pass/fail/inconclusive/not_applicable states. The demo command separately verifies its expected negative cases. Unknown schema versions are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Declare resource limits and measure repeatable performance for the supported workload in the pinned environment.
requirements.rationale: A tool that hangs or silently drops large input cannot be trusted in an engineering workflow.
requirements.acceptance: During M0 freeze input-size/case limits and a target runtime with machine details. M4 records actual elapsed time and peak memory; an oversized input or elapsed-time limit produces a bounded error and incomplete result. CAD work runs in a killable worker. Compare against the baseline; do not claim universal performance.

requirements.requirement: Keep offline workflows local by default and document dependency, fixture, manual, and example licensing.
requirements.rationale: Engineers must be able to inspect data handling and legally reuse the code and examples.
requirements.acceptance: No credentials or telemetry are needed; the offline demo completes with egress disabled after installation. Source examples have provenance and redistributable licenses, or use a download recipe and lawful independently authored fixtures. Escape user text in HTML; reject output path traversal and avoid executing input data.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate adoption from a separate clean consumer directory using only the documented public interface.
requirements.rationale: A successful bundled demo alone is not evidence that another engineer can use the tool.
requirements.acceptance: Record a complete cold-start walkthrough: install, configure one non-default input, get an expected failure, correct it, and reproduce success without editing package source. Include actual commands, setup time, code/config size, and limitations versus the baseline. Label agent-executed walkthroughs as such; practitioner validation remains unverified until real feedback exists.

exclusions.rationale: Manufacturer prose and undocumented behavior cannot be validated reliably from a small benchmark.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: A replacement for PyMeasure, QCoDeS, PyVISA, or a hardware abstraction platform
exclusions.rationale: Integrating one ecosystem is feasible and lowers adoption cost.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: Automatic discovery or writes to real instruments
exclusions.rationale: The first release is an offline test tool; real-device behavior needs a separately reviewed setup.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: Full Modbus TCP/RTU stack, every vendor, or universal SCPI compliance
exclusions.rationale: The register example checks PDU semantics only; transport standards and vendor coverage require additional evidence.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: Claims that emulator conformance proves physical accuracy or instrument safety
exclusions.rationale: Physical calibration, hardware quirks, and safe operating limits are outside software simulation.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

priority_policy.should: Valuable after Must; omission needs an explicit rationale
